newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian parliament to urge state help for Norilsk.
newsitem.headline: Russian parliament to urge state help for Norilsk.

text.p: Russia's State Duma lower parliament house will vote Wednesday on a measure urging state support for the financially troubled Norilsk Nickel metals group and state control over part of the company.
The measure also criticised commercial bank Uneximbank's restructuring programme for RAO Norilsky Nickel, in which it holds a major stake.
It said Uneximbank's plans to restructure Norilsk by breaking it up were "inadmissible".

"This would lead to the break-up of the single technological structure...and to the loss of the government's right to regulate and control output of nickel and copper ore and platinum group metals," it said.

It called on the government to extend control over a Norilsk stake owned by Uneximbank, which acquired the stake in a shares-for-loans auction in 1995. Uneximbank controls a 38 percent stake in Norilsk, or 51 percent of voting shares.
The Duma measure also asked the government to carry out support measures outlined in a 1996 presidential decree.

The decree, signed by Boris Yeltsin last August, proposed delaying some debt repayments, cutting import duties on mining and other equipment and ordering state help in getting supplies to Norilsk workers living in remote northern regions.

Norilsk is burdened by wage arrears and huge debts to the government. The Duma proposal put the company's total debts to the federal and regional budgets at 1.4 trillion roubles and wage arrears at 1.3 trillion.
The Duma also plans to ask the Audit Chamber, an independent body, to look into issues of production, ownership and finances at Norilsk, and to present its findings on March 25.
